[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: program statements read like maths equations, timeless relations among values. Java rule: each statement changes the state (the values of variables and array entries), and the next statement starts from the changed state.
[1] misconception (M) -> StateChangeIgnoredAcrossPasses: wrong rule: Values changed by one pass of a loop (other than the loop variable) do not affect later passes. Right rule: Each pass starts from the state left by the previous pass, so a change in one pass carries into the next ones.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: the state of a program is the information needed to know what it will do next: the values of its variables (and array entries) and which statement runs next.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: in a program without arrays, knowing the variable values and the next statement determines what the program does next; arrays add one state component per element.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: statements in a block execute in order, first to last, so the state seen by each statement is the result of all earlier ones.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: the output from any point on is determined by the current state; equal states give the same future behaviour (apart from Math.random and input).
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: each assignment changes exactly one variable or one array element; tracing tracks these changes.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Without arrays the state is the values of the variables plus the next statement; each array element adds one more variable to the state.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: tracing (a trace table of the state after each step) is how programs are understood and debugged; with large arrays one checks invariants among state components instead.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Conservation: an invariant such as 'valcnt equals the number of true entries in found[]' holds after every pass; a change that breaks it signals a bug.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: trace the full state for small programs. When arrays make the state too large to track, reason with invariants and partial traces instead.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Each pass starts from the state left by the previous one. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: an accumulator is not reset between outer passes (sum declared before the row loop), so later rows include earlier rows' totals
